items.name: S&P 500 (VFV + SPY)
items.street: Strategists are split: earnings are still growing, but the market is leaning on a handful of AI names while yields and oil stay high.
items.take: Crowd mood on the S&P 500 is about as gloomy as it gets, while the index itself has barely pulled back. Your VFV and SPY move together, so this is the sentiment that matters most for you.

Debt and equity raising to fund AI build-out

TPU chips are seen as a $100B+ opportunity and a challenge to Nvidia
Stock looks oversold (RSI near 30) at about 24x forward earnings
items.name: Alphabet
items.street: Strong Buy from 62 analysts; average target about $421–431, roughly a third above Friday's $317 close. Q3 consensus: revenue about $127.5B (+25%), EPS about $3.
items.take: The crowd is divided into two camps: a Cloud blowout sends it higher, a capex hike sends it lower. Your call is about $13 below its $330 strike, so the Oct 28 reaction matters a lot for its value.

mood.summary: Investors are nervous. The Fear & Greed index has sat in Extreme Fear for two weeks, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 9 points, well below the long-run norm. The S&P 500 fell for a second week and is about 2.5% off its Oct 6 record, while the Nasdaq is about 6% off after its worst day since June on Oct 22. Worries centre on AI spending, oil above $110 on Middle East tensions, and a possible Fed hike in December. Very fearful readings have often come before rebounds, but they don't say when.

trending.note: Board as of Wednesday 4:10 PM ET; prices are the Oct 28 close, with after-hours quotes for names that reported after the bell (MSFT, GOOG, GOOGL, ORCL). Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: Oracle Corp.
items.about: Enterprise software and cloud infrastructure company.
items.why: Shares jumped roughly 10% from about $131 to the mid-$140s late in the session, with the move coming in the final hour. Posts circulating on the board cite long-term goals of at least $225B revenue and $21 EPS by fiscal 2030 plus a capital-spending peak in FY2027-28; posts say Alphabet's results then pulled the stock back after the close.

items.name: Microsoft Corp
items.about: Software, cloud (Azure) and AI company.
items.why: Microsoft reported fiscal Q1 after the close; posts citing the results say EPS was $4.89 vs $4.73 expected, revenue $92.8B vs $90B and Azure growth 48% vs 45% expected. The stock traded near $551 after hours versus a $530.23 regular-session close.

items.name: Alphabet Inc - Class C
items.about: Parent of Google, YouTube and Google Cloud.
items.why: Alphabet reported Q3 after the close: posts citing the release say revenue was $127.6B (about $128.2B expected) with Search and YouTube ads short of estimates, while Google Cloud ($30.7B) beat and capex ($51.4B) came in below expectations. The shares fell about 5% after hours to roughly $301.

items.name: SELLAS Life Sciences Group Inc
items.about: Clinical-stage biotech developing cancer immunotherapies, led by galinpepimut-S for leukemia.
items.why: The stock fell about 14.5% on heavy volume after trading above $12.8 earlier in the day. I could not confirm a news trigger; posts say the drop is tied to the long-awaited Phase 3 REGAL leukemia readout and to dilution and trial-timing worries, which are unconfirmed crowd claims.

items.name: ServiceNow Inc
items.about: Cloud workflow-automation software for enterprises.
items.why: Shares slid about 3.7% into the close as software names were weighed by the Alphabet and Microsoft results and the sector's AI-disruption worries; posts also mention heavy short-dated call buying at the $165 strike. I did not find a company-specific news item.

items.name: NVIDIA Corp
items.about: Designs GPUs and AI computing platforms.
items.why: Shares eased about 1.2% as investors waited on hyperscaler spending signals from Microsoft and Alphabet earnings; posts say Alphabet's lower-than-expected capex raised questions for chip demand, which is an unconfirmed read.

items.name: Wendy's Co
items.about: Fast-food burger chain, franchisor of Wendy's restaurants.
items.why: Shares rose about 15% after Trian Fund Management and partners proposed a non-binding $7.35-per-share cash offer for the shares they don't own, about a 20% premium to Tuesday's close, per an SEC filing. Posts say activist Blackwells Capital opposes the proposal and holders want a higher price; the stock is trading near the offer price.

items.name: Alphabet Inc Class A
items.about: Parent of Google, YouTube and Google Cloud (Class A shares).
items.why: Same catalyst as GOOG: Q3 results after the close showed Cloud and capex better than expected but total revenue, Search and YouTube ads below estimates, per posts quoting the release. The shares dropped about 5.5% after hours to near $303.

items.name: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc.
items.about: Video game publisher behind Grand Theft Auto, NBA 2K and Red Dead Redemption.
items.why: The stock slipped about 2.6% to the $195-196 area. Posts say reports of a roughly 210 GB PlayStation 5 download for Grand Theft Auto VI prompted the dip, and others cite the absence of GTA Online news; both are unconfirmed crowd claims.

items.name: Cerebras Systems Inc
items.about: AI chipmaker known for wafer-scale processors for training and inference.
items.why: Shares fell about 6.7% after dropping as low as $105.36 intraday. Posts say a short-seller report published today raised accounting and other allegations and that another insider lockup release is coming Nov 9, with earnings around Nov 12; those details are unconfirmed.

items.name: Boston Scientific Corp.
items.about: Medical device maker focused on cardiology, endoscopy and urology.
items.why: The stock fell about 5.8% to around $42, trading as low as $39.60 on volume far above usual. I could not confirm a company-specific catalyst; posts mention a late-session slide and a prior guidance cut earlier in 2026.

items.name: Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1
items.about: ETF that tracks the Nasdaq-100 index of large non-financial Nasdaq companies.
items.why: The fund edged up about 0.5% into the close, with holders watching Microsoft and Alphabet results and Wednesday's Fed decision; Alphabet's after-hours drop is a drag on the biggest holdings.

items.name: Netlist Inc
items.about: Memory-module maker that earns money from patent licensing and litigation.
items.why: Shares rose about 5% to $6.96, and posts say the recent $6.99 level is the highest close since December 2021. Posts point to patent litigation and licensing catalysts and a possible Nasdaq uplisting, none confirmed here.

items.name: Genmab - ADR
items.about: Danish biotech developing antibody-based cancer drugs.
items.why: The ADR surged about 29% after Genmab said the Phase 3 LiGeR-HN1 trial of petosemtamab plus Keytruda met both primary endpoints, cutting the risk of death by 50% in first-line PD-L1-positive head and neck cancer at the first interim analysis.

items.name: Wynn Resorts Ltd.
items.about: Operator of luxury casino resorts in Las Vegas, Macau and the Gulf.
items.why: Shares slipped about 1.4% toward 52-week lows; posts attribute the weakness to Iran and Middle East concerns and a big options put purchase, and discuss buybacks. I did not find a company-specific news item.

items.name: AXT Inc
items.about: Maker of compound-semiconductor substrates used in optical and AI-related chips.
items.why: Shares rose about 11.6% with earnings expected soon. Posts cite an analyst upgrade and a report that its Tongmei subsidiary is seeking to raise up to roughly $545 million via a private share sale; neither is confirmed here.

items.name: Oatly Group
items.about: Swedish oat-milk and plant-based dairy company.
items.why: The ADS dropped about 28% after Q3 results: revenue grew 9.1% to $243.1M and adjusted EBITDA rose to $9.4M, but the company cut its 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $16M-$20M, citing fuel and freight inflation, per a summary of the release.

items.name: Sterling Construction Company, Inc.
items.about: Heavy-civil, building and site-development contractor, including data-center projects.
items.why: Shares rose about 4.5% ahead of third-quarter results due after the close, with volume above average. Posts say the stock is far below its peak and note the last earnings miss was in 2023.

items.name: Intellia Therapeutics Inc
items.about: Clinical-stage gene-editing company developing CRISPR-based therapies.
items.why: Shares rose about 8.6% as gene-editing stocks gained after the FDA issued draft guidance letting developers file one application covering several versions of a patient-specific gene-editing therapy, per Stocktwits News. Peers PRME, BEAM, EDIT and CRSP also rose.

items.name: Direxion Daily S&P Biotech Bear 3X Shares
items.about: Leveraged ETF that seeks three times the inverse of the daily move of an S&P biotech index.
items.why: The fund fell about 5.5% as biotech stocks rose, which is what an inverse 3X product does; posts talk about a Fed-day biotech move (XBI) and traders entering and exiting short-term.
